local_market_longform:
Bend is its own market, and a cash sale here works differently than the national talking points suggest. Homes in Bend currently trade around a median of $720,000 and take roughly 41 days to go under contract, with about 26% of area sales closing in cash. When you need certainty instead of a drawn-out listing — a firm number and a date you choose — that local pace is exactly why selling directly makes sense.

The housing stock shapes everything about condition here. Bend runs heavily to early-1900s mill-town cottages and a large share of 1990s–2020s resort and tract construction, and each era carries its own repair realities. That matters because we price the house in front of us rather than asking you to renovate it first — the things a traditional buyer's inspector flags are the same things we already expect and account for.

Local conditions are the other factor a generic buyer ignores. Around Bend, the issues we see most are high-desert freeze-thaw cracking, wildfire exposure in the wildland-urban interface, and aging septic and well systems on the outskirts. We've made offers on homes with every one of those problems, so none of it scares us off or kills the deal at the last minute.

We buy across the whole area — from close-in neighborhoods like the Old Mill District out to Redmond and Sisters — and in Oregon the local economy anchored by outdoor-recreation tourism, remote-work in-migration, and a growing tech presence keeps demand real. Inherited homes, tired rentals, pre-foreclosure situations in Deschutes County, and houses that simply need more work than the owner wants to take on: those are the Bend sellers we help most.

Being a genuinely local buyer near the Cascade peaks and Mount Bachelor also means our offer isn't a lowball pulled from a national algorithm that has never seen Bend. We know what a block in the Old Mill District, Awbrey Butte, the Old Bend core, and Larkspur actually sells for, what Central Oregon buyers will and won't pay for, and how Deschutes County's title and closing process really works. That local read is why our sellers get a number they can trust and a closing that actually happens on the date we promised.

faq.q: How fast can you close on my Bend house?
faq.a: As little as 7 days through a licensed Oregon title company, or any later date you choose. Sellers in Bend pick the timeline that fits their move.

faq.q: Do I pay any fees or commissions?
faq.a: None. No agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover standard closing costs. The number we agree on is what you receive.

faq.q: Do I need to repair or clean the house first?
faq.a: No. We buy Bend homes in any condition — including the high-desert freeze-thaw cracking we see so often here. Take what you want and leave the rest.

faq.q: How do you decide the offer amount?
faq.a: We look at recent comparable sales in your Bend neighborhood — places like the Old Mill District — the home's condition, and current Central Oregon demand, then make a fair cash offer you're free to accept or decline.

faq.q: Is this a licensed, legitimate way to sell in Oregon?
faq.a: Yes. We are a direct buyer, not your agent or broker, and we put that in writing. Oregon requires wholesalers to register with the Oregon Real Estate Agency; we buy directly and disclose our role and intent on every contract.

faq.q: Can you help with foreclosure, probate, or tenants?
faq.a: Often, yes. We regularly work with Deschutes County sellers facing foreclosure, probate, liens, or tenant issues, and we structure the sale around the situation.
